las-b14-001.name: Hyttfallets bruk
las-b14-001.evidence: SHIP-BLOCKING (name overlap, same domain). Hyttfallet is a real, documented Swedish ironworking site: the rapids at Hyttfallet in Hammarby, Nora bergslag (Örebro county) were dammed from the early 1500s; Gustav Vasa's Kungshammaren was built there in 1544, Gislehyttan operated 1602–1698, the site developed into Hammarby bruk, and the works ran until 1923 — i.e. a charcoal-iron works active through exactly the later-1800s period the passage describes, and documented by Länsstyrelsen Örebro and Noraskogs hembygdsförening. The candidate attaches fabricated charcoal accounts across forty-two years, invented crofter delivery ledgers and an invented 1868 charge for undelivered stig to an ironworks named 'Hyttfallets bruk'. Mitigating facts for the adjudicator: the real works' formal name is Hammarby bruk (Hyttfallet names the rapid, not the company), and 'hyttfall' is a descriptive compound (smelter + waterfall) that could in principle recur. Recommend rename regardless — a Swedish reader searching 'Hyttfallet bruk' lands on the real Nora site.
